_comment: The GitLab project Oneshot works in, and the two labels that are its entire external state. Verified against gitlab.arbisoft.com on 2026-08-25: project id 1491, 16 labels, dev/stage/master protected with can_push=false.
_comment_context: The work repo's own main checkout. Worktrees are cut from it and its node_modules/venv are linked into each one; phases NEVER write to it or run git in it — hooks/write-scope.js and git-guard.js deny both for every phase. Skills, agents and rules do not come from here: they live in this repo's harness/ (ONESHOT_SKILLS_ROOT), and the checkout's own .claude/ is hidden from every worktree so harness/ is the only one a phase sees (src/lib/worktrees.ts). Oneshot needs exactly two repositories on a machine: this one and the work repo.
_comment_labels: ONE label in, one label out. There is no intermediate state machine — progress lives in the Slack card and the run journal, not on the board. All three ids below already exist on project 1491; Oneshot never creates, renames or deletes a label. 'review' is a FOURTH, OPTIONAL label, never required and never swapped by Oneshot: a ticket carrying it alongside 'Loop' gets three extra human sign-off pauses (see README's 'Optional human review gates'). Its id is not yet verified against the live project (create the label there before relying on it) — the code only ever checks label MEMBERSHIP by name, never the id, so an unverified id costs nothing.
_comment_reviewAllRuns: TRUE = the review gates apply to EVERY run, not only tickets carrying the Review label or touching highScrutinyPaths. This is a deliberate change of posture: with it on, every run pauses after `plan` and after `testcases` for a human, and never merges its own MR. The label and the path list still work and are still worth keeping — they are what makes a gate survive this being switched back off. Requires channels:history (or groups:history) on the Slack bot token; without it every gate sits 'pending' forever and every run parks, which is why doctor FAILS rather than warns while this is true.
_comment_high_scrutiny: Paths the ERP's own .claude/rules/security.md marks 'escalate immediately'. A ticket whose PLAN or DIFF touches one gets the Review gates even without the Review label, because the label is human-applied and therefore forgettable — and the tickets most worth pausing on are exactly the ones nobody remembers to label. Matching is a plain substring test against repo-relative paths, so 'apps/payroll/' catches everything under it. Empty this array to switch the behaviour off entirely. Note the last two entries: authentication on the FRONTEND has no single directory the way apps/auth/ does, so its entry points are listed by name. Found the hard way — ticket #8 is an auth-context bug with 600+ production occurrences, and a backend-only list would not have gated it.
_comment_markers: Persistent labels Oneshot must copy through untouched on any label write. A label swap is one update_issue call carrying the full array, so anything not listed here and not the entry/exit label would be silently dropped.
_comment_branches: base is what ticket branches are cut from and what their MRs target. NOTE: the project's GitLab default branch is 'main', NOT 'dev' — do not infer the base from the default branch. 'main' is protected but currently reports can_push=true for our token, which is why it is in protectedBranches: the guard must refuse it even though the server would allow it.
_comment_promotion: dev is FINAL. A ticket MR merges into base and the run is done — nothing is promoted onward. dev -> stage is deliberately absent rather than auto:false, because auto:false reads as 'a human owns this hop' (which is what it means for stage -> master) and that is not the reason here: the hop is switched off while the pipeline earns trust. With no entry whose `from` is the base branch, runPromotions() records no promotion and merge reports 'no automatic promotion applies to this base'. Restore by putting { from: dev, to: stage, auto: true } back — nothing else has to change, and note that config/deploy.json already ships dev (defaultRef), so the deploy never depended on this hop. stage -> master stays listed and stays manual: production release is a human act.
_comment_concurrency: In-flight TICKET cap. The old MUST-STAY-1 constraint is now carried by the promotion mutex (src/lib/promotion.ts): the deploy script ships the TIP of dev, so exactly one run may occupy the merge→deploy→qa window at a time — that is where attribution lives, and the mutex enforces it while every other phase pipelines freely. Residual cap reasons: worktrees symlink ONE shared node_modules/venv (a second webpack build during another run's verify contends on the babel cache), and the port pool (PORT_POOL, default 3) bounds server-holding phases. Raise toward the pool size once shared-cache contention is observed to be tolerable. Set to 1 deliberately: the operator runs one ticket per loop and scales by starting more conductors, so the fleet-wide ceiling is PORT_POOL and each process holds exactly one run — which also keeps the shared node_modules/venv contention this comment warns about at one build per conductor.
